item.title: How these young Nigerians turned their class project into a solution that helps with house rents
item.description: Founded by three young Nigerians who experienced Lagos’ rent shock firsthand, Ule Homes is challenging Nigeria’s broken rental system by turning lump-sum rent into manageable monthly payments.

item.title: Angosat-2 goes commercial for startups and ISPs in Angola
item.description: On Techpoint Digest, we discuss Angosat-2's commercial launch for startups and ISPs, Ule Homes' efforts to solve Nigeria's rent problem, and X's lawsuit against a startup attempting to revive Twitter.

item.title: Timilehin Ayantunji never studied computer science, but he’s helping shape how millions of Nigerians move money
item.description: Timilehin Ayantunji started out learning frontend development on YouTube. Today, he has worked on telemedicine products, digital banking features, accelerator platforms, and mobile money solutions used across Nigeria.

item.title: Why GoLemon’s Chowdeck deal could quickly backfire
item.description: GoLemon’s partnership with Chowdeck promises faster delivery, but it may quietly hand over initiative, turning GoLemon from a destination into a supplier.

item.title: From Huwaei to Airtel and 9Mobile, Ibikunle Peters explains how he spent 10 years ensuring phone calls go through
item.description: Ibikunle Peters has spent over 10 years making sure calls go through at different telcos. He shares how he works, and what it took to land a job at top telecom companies.

item.title: Why this Franco-Beninese founder built his fintech in Nigeria, and not in France or the Benin Republic
item.description: In this edition of After Hours, we follow Achille Arouko and how his early encounters with computers in Benin Republic, formal training in France, and exposure to Nigeria’s tech ecosystem shaped his decision to build Bujeti in Lagos.

item.description: From why accelerators matter to how founders should choose the right programme, this article breaks down the role of startup accelerators in Africa and profiles 10 of the most important programmes shaping the continent’s next generation of startups.

item.description: Master the top 10 tech skills for 2026. From AI engineering to cybersecurity, discover high-demand skills that boost earning potential and job security.
